headline: Working Missourians can’t afford hidden hospital contract games
summary: The article discusses issues with restrictive contract clauses in health plans that limit competition among hospitals and drive up costs. Missouri hospitals should compete based on quality and price, with health funds able to choose providers freely. These clauses may impact state healthcare expenditure through increased costs.

headline: Note to the Ohio legislature: Many school districts are in fiscal trouble.
summary: The Ohio legislature's expansion of charter schools and vouchers is straining public education budgets, with over 120 districts trimming budgets due to reduced state support. Lawmakers, including House Speaker Matt Huffman and Senate Education Chair Andrew Brenner, have pushed these policies despite constitutional concerns and financial strain on public schools.

headline: As Idaho extends slim budgets and feds shift stance, disability care may face cuts, advocates worry
summary: Idaho faces budget tightness, with potential cuts to Medicaid's home and community-based services. Federal changes could allow states to shift people with disabilities to institutions, but Idaho lacks sufficient institutional capacity. Lawmakers narrowly avoided broader cuts this year, but approved $22 million in cuts to residential habilitation services. State agencies are preparing for reduced funding in the next legislative session.

headline: As shortfall looms, Pillen installs allies on board meant to keep politics out of budget forecast
summary: Governor Jim Pillen reshaped the Nebraska Economic Forecasting Advisory Board by replacing three members, including its longest-serving member, with appointees who previously supported his tax cuts. Critics worry this move may politicize the board and impact its objective revenue forecasts, which could affect Nebraska's state budget. The board's October projections will help Pillen craft his budget proposal for lawmakers in January, with the state currently projected to face a $208 million deficit in 2027.

headline: Cold shoulder: Brattleboro won’t be welcoming ICE
summary: Brattleboro Police Chief Jeremy Evans stated his department will not collaborate with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers, including refusing entry to their facility and notifying the public if ICE is present in town. This stance was supported by local residents and organizations who called for stronger policies protecting immigrants, urging the police to abide by the Fair and Impartial Policing Policy and resist any partnerships with federal ICE agents. The police chief expressed discomfort with the South Burlington ICE raid, emphasizing that the Brattleboro Police Department will not enter into agreements with ICE.

headline: Barre schools eye cuts to sports and other activities after budget fails on third attempt
summary: Barre Unified Union School District faces budget crisis as voters reject $57.1M budget proposal for the third time, leading to potential cuts in winter sports, transportation, and extracurricular activities. The district is the last in Vermont without a voter-approved budget, which may result in up to $22,000 monthly interest payments. The state's education funding model complexity contributes to budget disagreements.

headline: Roxbury warehouse again at center of ICE detention fight
summary: Immigrant advocates allege U.S. Department of Homeland Security is using a Roxbury warehouse for migrant detention despite a court order prohibiting such use. New Jersey's Attorney General is investigating reports of ICE activity at the warehouse.

headline: Quinnipiac poll has Lamont with double digit lead over Fazio
summary: The Quinnipiac University poll shows Connecticut Governor Ned Lamont leading Republican challenger Ryan Fazio by 17 points, with women strongly favoring Lamont. Fazio, seeking to unseat a governor for the first time since 1954, requested more debates but Lamont's campaign agreed to two televised events. Lamont faces lower enthusiasm for his reelection bid, with only 27% of his voters being very enthusiastic, compared to 39% for Fazio.

headline: Four rural CT hospitals receive $46 million in federal health grants
summary: Connecticut's rural hospitals received $46 million in federal grants to enhance imaging, telehealth, and transport services. Day Kimball Hospital, facing financial struggles, will use its $20.2 million share to improve access to care. The state received a total of $154 million, with $104 million allocated for various projects, including healthcare workforce development and maternity services.

headline: Lamont administration signals universal free school lunch is still on the menu
summary: Connecticut Lt. Gov. Susan Bysiewicz announced plans to expand free meals in schools, following a successful universal breakfast program. She aims to provide free lunches to all public school students by 2027, potentially costing the state millions more. This expansion could ease financial burdens for families and reduce stigma around free meal programs, as seen with the universal breakfast initiative. The Republican gubernatorial challenger, Sen. Ryan Fazio, expressed skepticism towards universal free lunches but is open to proposals.

headline: Mothers, reproductive rights group sue Oklahoma officials over abortion ban
summary: Two Oklahoma mothers, Magon Hoffman and Sheena Hamlin, sued state leaders challenging abortion restrictions after they had to leave the state for terminations due to fatal fetal diagnoses. The lawsuit argues that Oklahoma's abortion bans violate pregnant women's rights to life, liberty, and equal protection.

headline: State Treasury flagged $1.4B in improper payments; lawmakers say greater oversight needed
summary: Pennsylvania's State Treasurer identified and blocked $1.4 billion in improper payments in FY 2026. Two senators plan legislation requiring agencies to assess and report on improper payments every two years, aiming to curb waste and improve transparency. This initiative may impact state budget by potentially reducing improper spending.

headline: Residents push back against planned Nashville ICE coordination center
summary: Dozens of Nashville residents protested plans to establish an ICE enforcement support center in their city, citing concerns about immigration policies and community surveillance. The protest took place at a Nashville Metro Council meeting, with residents urging council members to intervene against the center's presence. The contract for the center was awarded to Alaska-based Koniag Services, with federal documents showing it could cost up to $63 million.

headline: Trump administration has cut or frozen $177 billion in grants across every state, analysis shows
summary: The Trump administration has cut or frozen up to $177 billion in federal grants since the president's second term, impacting all 50 states, including Mississippi. These cuts could potentially strain state budgets, as they rely on federal funds for various services.

headline: Kansans warned about increased rabies cases in bats and other animals
summary: Kansas health authorities warn of increased bat rabies cases, urging clinicians to conduct risk assessments before administering post-exposure prophylaxis. CDC reports nationwide uptick in rabies exposures and assessments.
